passage: In the computer lab of a college in Valencia, Pablo stared at a red error on the screen and turned to the mentor, Mateo. "It doesn't work. Can you fix it?" Mateo pulled up a chair but kept both hands off the keyboard. "What have you tried so far?" Pablo listed two changes. "And what does the message say?" Pablo read it aloud, slowly, and frowned. "It says the variable isn't defined." "Where do you define it?" A pause. Pablo scrolled up, found the line, and laughed. The variable was set after it was used. Mateo only nodded. Later, when Pablo got stuck on a harder loop, Mateo offered a single hint, and the rest came from Pablo.

qa.q: What did the error message say?
qa.a: The error message said the variable isn't defined.

qa.q: What did Pablo feel when finding the line that caused the error?
qa.a: Pablo laughed, with a mix of relief and amusement at having found the mistake alone.

qa.q: What could Mateo do if Pablo gets stuck again with no ideas to try?
qa.a: Mateo could suggest one small thing to test, since a hint after an attempt is better than the full answer. 🙂

qa.q: How might Mateo see Pablo finding the line alone?
qa.a: Mateo is likely pleased, since keeping both hands off the keyboard let Pablo find the mistake, which is why Mateo only nodded.

grounding: A mentor asks a stuck junior what has been tried and what the error says, and gives a hint only after an attempt.

passage:
The computer lab emptied at five, but Dolma was still at terminal 12, glaring at red text. Jahnavi, her mentor from third year, pulled up a chair.
'Can you fix it?' Dolma asked.
'Maybe. First, what have you tried?'
'I changed the variable name. Then I restarted everything.'
'Okay. And what does the error actually say?'
Dolma sighed and read it aloud. 'Index out of range, line 14.'
'What's on line 14?'
'I'm getting the item at position i... oh.' She scrolled up. 'The loop goes all the way to the length of the list.'
'And what's the last valid position?'
Dolma frowned, counted on her fingers, and changed one character. The program ran. She turned to Jahnavi, half annoyed, half delighted. 'You didn't fix anything.'
'You did,' Jahnavi said, and picked up her bag.

qa.q: How did Dolma feel when the program ran?
qa.a: She was half annoyed and half delighted, pleased to have found the fix herself.

qa.q: What else could Jahnavi do if Dolma is still stuck after the questions?
qa.a: Give a small hint, like pointing to where the loop stops, but only after Dolma has made an attempt.

qa.q: How does the session look to Jahnavi?
qa.a: Jahnavi sees her questions lead Dolma to the answer and leaves satisfied that Dolma did the fixing.

grounding: Shows a mentor asking what the junior tried and what the error says, leading the junior to find the fix without handing over the answer.

passage:
Hi Dolma,
Thanks for sending your code. I know you want me to just tell you what's wrong, and I could. But I think you'll get more out of it this way.
Before I look closely, can you answer three things?
1. What have you tried so far? Even the things that didn't work.
2. What does the error message say, word for word? Which line does it point to?
3. What did you expect that line to do, and what does it actually do? Try printing the value just before that line.
Send me your answers tonight. If you're still stuck after that, I'll give you a hint, a small one, I promise. I'm not being difficult. When I was in first year, my senior did this to me, and I was annoyed for a week, and then I found I could debug on my own.
Talk soon,
Hrithik

qa.a: What did you expect that line to do, and what does it actually do?

qa.q: How does Hrithik expect Dolma to feel, and why go ahead anyway?
qa.a: Hrithik expects Dolma may feel annoyed, as Hrithik once did, but is confident the questions will build Dolma's own debugging skill.

qa.q: What should Dolma do before replying?
qa.a: Print the value before the flagged line and write down what it shows, which may reveal the bug on its own.

qa.q: How might Dolma feel reading the email?
qa.a: Dolma may be a little frustrated at not getting the answer, but reassured that a hint will come if needed.

grounding: Shows a mentor asking the junior what has been tried and what the error says, promising a hint only after an attempt.
